Dubai's airport saw passenger traffic drop 31% in the first half of 2026 to 31.5 million, down from 46 million, after Iran War triggered closures, cancellations, and airspace restrictions across the Gulf.
March was the low point with a 65% year-on-year drop.
Only about 50 of the usual 90 international airlines were operating by mid-year. 
The airport had been on track for 100 million passengers after a record 95.2 million in 2025.
Source: Reuters

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
France is pushing to limit Ukraine's ability to buy non-European military equipment with EU loan money, seeking to steer the €60 billion defense portion of the EU's €90 billion support package toward European and French producers.
Ukraine has secured two exemptions so far: one for Chinese drone components and another for US Patriot interceptor missiles. 
France wants these exemptions to be temporary, with European suppliers replacing foreign ones as production ramps up.
Nine EU countries including Germany, Sweden, and Poland pushed back, calling for Ukraine to have "maximum flexibility to procure the equipment it urgently needs."
France has a clear commercial interest: its Franco-Italian SAMP/T system is Europe's closest alternative to the US Patriot.
Source: Euronews

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Russia's new jet-powered Shahed drones fly at 300 mph, three times faster than the classic propeller version, and they exist because of Chinese engines.
Ukrainian wreckage analysis traces the turbojets to Shenzhen-based Telefly Telecommunications Equipment. 
After Ukraine publicized the link, Telefly removed the turbojet section from its English website. 
It remained on Chinese-language pages.
The jet variants are a serious problem because Ukraine intercepts over 90% of the slow propeller Shaheds with cheap drones. 
The jet versions outrun those interceptors and require scarce missiles or fighter jets to stop.
Chinese-origin parts now make up roughly 60-65% of recovered Shaheds. 
Beijing maintains it does not send "lethal weapons," classifying the components as dual-use. 
Some engines were shipped disguised as industrial refrigeration units.
Source: WSJ

Australia’s reliance on U.S.-made missiles is becoming a strategic vulnerability as the Iran war drains American stockpiles. 
Analysts warn deliveries of weapons such as Tomahawks could be delayed, leaving Australia exposed in a potential Indo-Pacific conflict.
Canberra is accelerating domestic missile production, with new factories planned and locally made Naval Strike and Joint Strike Missiles expected from 2027. 
But critics say Australia is still moving too slowly and remains heavily dependent on U.S. supplies.
Source: POLITICO

✡️🇮🇱 From the West Bank to Syria: how Israel uses herds to seize land
Israel has quietly introduced a herd of 140 cattle onto Syrian land near the Golan Heights, using what appears to be a rural outpost to expand its territorial grip under the cover of agriculture.
🔴 Israeli forces have erected approximately 22 kilometers of fencing, some of it electrified, and have placed the land under military protection
🔴 IDF officers directly guided operations, providing settlers with marked locations of land for seizure
🔴 Syrian farmers report that they have been cut off from their land, with the military firing at anyone who approaches
This operation mirrors a strategy perfected in the West Bank, where so-called "shepherding outposts" have been used to claim land. According to the Syrian monitor Sijil, these methods have facilitated the takeover of over 10,000 hectares in the West Bank, close to a fifth of the entire territory. The practice has displaced Palestinians across 97 communities and areas since January 2023, most of them Bedouin and herding communities.
👉 The economic impact has been devastating. Farmers have been forced to sell livestock, take on debt, and, in some cases, sell personal assets just to cover basic needs.
The Syrian monitoring group Sijjil documented 187 violations in July and 239 in June, ranging from ground incursions to raids. Locals stress that tactics are designed to create an environment that drives people out.
The land seizure is part of a broader Israeli strategy to reshape the region. The "Greater Israel" project, which has been openly discussed by Israeli leaders, envisions expanding borders to include territory in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, and Iraq.

🤔 Turkey moves to bring Kurds into its orbit as US influence wanes
Turkey is pressing ahead with a strategic opening toward its Kurdish population, betting that a peace deal could extend the country's influence well beyond its borders, The Cradle reports.
The window of opportunity opened after the US reliance on the "Kurdish card," a strategic tool it has used since the Cold War, failed against Iran.
🔴 US was unable to mobilize either the Kurds of Iran or the larger Kurdish groups in Iraq, despite decades of investment in those relationships.
🔴 In Syria, the US-backed Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) have collapsed, with their geopolitical project of building an autonomous Kurdish region now largely dismantled as the US steps aside
This has created a strategic opening for Turkey. It has eliminated the military and territorial threat posed by armed Kurdish groups in Syria, advancing its goal of subordinating the region and expanding its influence eastward.
The Kurdish opening is part of a broader Turkish strategy to establish itself as the dominant power in West Asia:
🔴 Turkey has signed a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, signaling its ambition to lead an emerging Sunni-majority bloc
🔴 Turkey is seeking to expand its influence from the Caspian Sea to the Mediterranean, positioning itself as a central player in the region's new security architecture
🔴 It is deepening economic and military ties across the region, including drone sales, military academies, and scholarships that build lasting influence
At home, President Erdogan has a huge stake in making sure the peace plan succeeds. He aims to dissolve the decade-old opposition bloc led by the pro-Kurdish DEM Party and the Republican People's Party, which stand in the way of prolonging his already protracted tenure. Erdogan has been courting the DEM Party to help change the constitution and secure additional terms in exchange for enhanced recognition of Kurdish rights.
👉 However, opposition voices warn that Erdogan's gestures of peace toward Kurds are little more than a political ploy to gain popularity and extend his term in office.
For decades, the Kurdish conflict has been a domestic headache for Turkey. Now, Turkish leaders see an opportunity to turn the Kurdish issue into an instrument of regional influence. If Turkey can pacify its own Kurdish population, it will also position itself as the dominant power over Kurdish groups in Syria and Iraq, locking in Turkish influence across the region.
